cues.zh: 我们还能做几件事：我们明知加锁是个问题，但其实大部分锁并没有竞争，

cues.en: that's like in 99% case.
cues.zh: 大概 99% 的情况下都是如此。

cues.en: So you need an atomic operation, a CAS, to go take a lock in the first place but usually it's never contended. So we wanted the uncontended CAS to be fast so we arranged our hardware memory model such that an uncontended CAS can hit in your L1 cache and it runs at an L1 cache speed.
cues.zh: 起初你需要一个原子操作（即 CAS）去获取锁，但通常根本没有竞争。所以我们希望无竞争的 CAS 能足够快，为此我们设计了硬件内存模型，让无竞争的 CAS 能直接命中 L1 缓存，以 L1 缓存的速度运行。

cues.en: So CAS can hit in cache, it's a one clock pipeline. Same thing for memory fence. If you don't have any outstanding memory references that aren't going to be resolvable and there's no contention for memory, you can do a memory fence, a proper Java memory model ordering in a clock pipeline,
cues.zh: 这样 CAS 就能命中缓存，只需一个时钟周期的流水线。内存屏障也是同理。只要你没有无法解析的未完成内存引用，且没有内存竞争，你就能在一个流水线周期内完成一次内存屏障，实现符合 Java 内存模型的定序，

cues.en: right? Turns out that CAS, as implemented by every other CPU on the planet, includes a memory fence
cues.zh: 对吧？但事实证明，地球上其他所有 CPU 实现的 CAS，都自带了内存屏障，

cues.en: and that memory fence is not the correct spot for how a hotspot does locks, so hotspot emits a second fence on top of the CAS as part of the standard cost of taking a Java lock.
cues.zh: 而那个内存屏障的位置，并不符合 HotSpot 处理锁的方式，所以 HotSpot 会在 CAS 之上再插入第二个屏障，作为获取 Java 锁的常规开销。

cues.en: It's kind of a painful thing. So we have a no fence CAS and we turned out we found a bunch of other interesting use cases for this atomic updated performance counters, a bunch of lock free algorithms which don't need ordering. So we use this NoFence CAS all over the place and it makes us sort of run faster in this highly contended, highly concurrent code.
cues.zh: 这确实挺让人头疼的。所以我们做了一个无屏障的 CAS（NoFence CAS），结果发现它还有很多有趣的用例，比如原子更新性能计数器，以及一堆不需要定序的无锁算法。我们在各处都用上了这种 NoFence CAS，它让我们在高竞争、高并发的代码中跑得更快。

cues.en: We do have fences
cues.zh: 我们确实有内存屏障，

cues.en: to force ordering when we need it. There's not otherwise much ordering. It's a much weaker memory model than say,
cues.zh: 用于在需要时强制保序。除此以外基本没有定序限制。相比之下，这是一个弱得多的内存模型，比如对比

cues.en: x86s
or Sparks TSO.

cues.zh: 我们允许各种其他内存模型禁止的重排序，并依赖屏障来保证结果正确，运行 Java 代码的 JIT 自然会正确处理这些，从而让你获得符合规范的 Java 内存模型。好的。

cues.en: So we've had hardware transactional memory support in from day one. I must a little bit talk about what goes on with this.

cues.en: There are extra opcodes, the speculate, commit and abort opcodes and
cues.zh: 有额外的操作码：speculate、commit 和 abort 操作码，以及

cues.en: there's extra tag bits in your L1 cache. And there's nothing at all in your L2 about how the HTM works. The hardware guys are very clear on that. You cannot the L2 is what Intel calls the LLC, the last level cache. It's the point of coherency
cues.zh: L1 缓存里还有额外的标记位。而 L2 里完全没有关于 HTM 如何工作的东西。硬件团队对这一点非常明确。你不能碰它——L2 就是 Intel 所说的 LLC，最后一级缓存。它是系统中成百上千个 CPU 之间的一致性点

cues.en: between the hundreds and hundreds of CPUs in the system. That is already one of the most complicated parts of the system. So nothing on the L2 on hardware transactional memory, it's all done in the L1 level. So when you start and end a transaction,
cues.zh: 那已经是系统里最复杂的部分之一了。你绝不可能跑进去加一个没人知道有没有用的奇怪新东西。所以硬件事务内存在 L2 上什么都没有，全都在 L1 层完成。所以当你开始和结束一个事务时，

cues.en: whether it succeeds or fails or whatever it does, the L2 is utterly unaware that you're doing this, right? Okay. So you have extra tag bits in your L1, you turn on the speculate mode with the speculate opcode.
cues.zh: 不管它是成功、失败还是怎样，L2 完全不知道你在做这件事，对吧？好。所以你的 L1 里有额外的标记位，你用 speculate 操作码开启推测模式。

cues.en: Every time you do a read or write, it tests it sets a little bit in the L1 cache saying, This line has been read speculatively or written speculatively.
cues.zh: 每次读或写时，它都会检查并在 L1 缓存里设置一个标记位，表示：这一行是被推测性读取或推测性写入的。

cues.en: And then if you ever lose a line, one of these tag lines out of your L1 for whatever reason, you abort.
cues.zh: 然后如果你因为任何原因丢失了 L1 中的某一行——也就是这些带标记的行之一——你就会中止。

cues.en: And if you abort, you lose them all. We just take all the spec lines and throw them out of the cache. So all those rights you accumulated in your, you know, L1 cache, they all thrown out. And then you go to a software recovery mechanism which
cues.zh: 而一旦中止，你就全丢了。我们会把所有推测性缓存行直接扔出缓存。于是你在 L1 缓存里积累的那些写入，全都被丢掉了。然后你进入软件恢复机制，它会

cues.en: essentially decides to retry the transaction or switch to heavyweight lock or do something, whatever do whatever it's going to do to recover the situation.
cues.zh: 基本上就是决定重试事务、切换到重量级锁，还是做点别的——不管它要用什么办法来恢复局面。

cues.en: Since you're doing Java level locking, it's entirely plausible
cues.zh: 既然你是在 Java 层面做锁，那完全有可能

cues.en: to do software recovery where you just retry the lock a few times and see if you can't get the transaction to float through.
cues.zh: 用软件恢复：把锁重试几次，看看能不能让事务顺利通过。

cues.en: and the true data dependency prevents all kinds of transactional memory, hardware, software, whatever you're going do, you have a true data And usually that true data dependency is due to something stupid like a performance counter that's no one's looking at. But you add one to a shared counter, it's a true data dependency and you're stuck. You just can't make that transact.
cues.zh: 而真正的数据依赖会阻止所有类型的事务内存——硬件、软件、不管你要做什么，你都有一个真正的数据依赖。而且通常这个真正的数据依赖是因为某个没人看的性能计数器之类的蠢东西。但你只要往共享计数器上加一，它就是真正的数据依赖，你就卡住了。你就是没法把它事务化。

cues.en: So someone has to hack the code. As soon as someone's willing to hack the code, by the way, then all bets are off. Why hack your code to make it transactional memory friendly when you could hack it to be fine grained locking friendly? Absolutely.
cues.zh: 所以必须有人去改代码。顺便说一句，一旦有人愿意改代码，那情况就完全变了。既然能改成对细粒度锁友好，为什么还要改成对事务内存友好呢？确实如此。

cues.en: Yeah,
cues.zh: 没错，

cues.en: already done. It's in high scale lib. And
cues.zh: 已经做好了，就在 HighScaleLib 里。而且

cues.en: it turns out that in practice, when we get to these high CPU counts, big box systems,
cues.zh: 事实证明在实际应用中，当我们面对这种多 CPU、大型机系统时，

cues.en: what prevents scaling is GC, it's not locking.
cues.zh: 阻碍扩展的是 GC，而不是锁。

cues.en: People write
cues.zh: 大家写的代码……

cues.en: they have GC issues that they consume more memory or have a large enough heap that they have GC pause times that prevent them from trying to make a bigger system because the pauses are killing them as it is. So instead they cluster smaller JVMs,
cues.zh: 他们遇到了 GC 问题，内存消耗过大或堆太大导致 GC 停顿时间过长，以至于不敢做更大的系统，因为现有的停顿就已经要命了。所以他们转而搞小型 JVM 集群，

cues.en: right?
cues.zh: 对吧？

cues.en: Oh, yeah, contrast this to Sun Niagara Rock product.
cues.zh: 哦对了，再对比一下 Sun 的 Niagara Rock 产品。

cues.en: We do not abort for function calls or TLB misses or nested locks or a thousand other things that Rock does. We have a much stronger implementation than Sun's Rock processor,
cues.zh: 我们不会因为函数调用、TLB 未命中、嵌套锁或 Rock 会遇到的另外上千种情况而中止。我们的实现比 Sun 的 Rock 处理器要强健得多，

cues.en: much weaker than most academic paper
cues.zh: 但比大多数学术论文里的构想要弱很多，

cues.en: presentations that never see the light of day but it doesn't matter.
cues.zh: 那些方案永远无法面世，不过这并不重要。

cues.en: It's not going to save the world. Okay.
cues.zh: 它又拯救不了世界。好了。

cues.en: What other things are going on here? It's the time let's think back to 2000, 2002, we're designing a system. Okay, the multi core obvious risk
cues.zh: 这里还有什么门道呢？让我们回想一下 2000、2002 年那会儿，我们正在设计一个系统。多核架构显而易见的风险是，

cues.en: is you're to run out of bandwidth because each one of these CPUs is going to have its own, you know,
cues.zh: 你的带宽会被耗尽，因为每一个 CPU 都会有它自己的……

cues.en: working set of memory it's going to touch, its own set of cache misses, it's got these relatively small cache that's going to need to go to memory a lot, you're to run out of bandwidth, right? You're to have 54 cores, you're going have 54 as much bandwidth requirement, well not quite, but something like that. So it turns out that we have a bunch of things we can do. We did
cues.zh: 要访问的内存工作集，有各自的缓存未命中，而且缓存相对较小，需要频繁访问内存，带宽就会耗尽，对吧？如果有 54 个核心，带宽需求就会是 54 倍，好吧，虽然没那么夸张，但也差不多。所以事实上我们有很多事情可以做。我们做了

cues.en: what we call a CLZ instruction, the just in time zeroing in your L1 cache.
cues.zh: 一种我们称之为 CLZ 的指令，在 L1 缓存中进行即时清零。

cues.en: It's support for streaming memory allocation. It turns out that if you look at how standard garbage collectors do allocation, it's this very efficient bump pointer style allocation
cues.zh: 它为流式内存分配提供了支持。事实证明，如果你看看标准垃圾回收器是如何做内存分配的，就会发现它用的是这种非常高效的指针碰撞式分配，

cues.en: but that also means that you're constantly moving to new addresses that have never been seen by this CPU since the last full GC cycle. So long ago, those addresses all left your cache. So it's a constant stream of cache misses.
cues.zh: 但这也意味着你在不断移动到新地址，而这些地址自上次 Full GC 周期以来就没被这个 CPU 访问过。很久以前，那些地址就已经全被移出缓存了。所以这会导致源源不断的缓存未命中。

cues.en: You promptly zero that memory by writing it entirely and then you fill it with good data and use it for a while and then most of it dies young in your cache because the generational assumption works and most objects die young. Okay, fine. But what it means is you read a bunch of stuff from memory in order to touch this new cache line that you promptly zeroed. So you didn't actually need to do the read. You don't want that data, you're to fill it with zeros. You just want coherence.
cues.zh: 你会立即将那块内存全部写零，然后填入有效数据并使用一段时间，接着大部分对象就会在缓存中夭折，因为分代假说是成立的，大部分对象朝生夕灭。行，这没问题。但这意味为了访问这个你马上就要清零的新缓存行，你先从内存中读取了一堆东西。所以你根本不需要去读。你不需要那些数据，你只是要把它填满零。你需要的仅仅是一致性。

cues.en: So we have this just in time zeroing which zeros the line in the cache without actually reading memory, lowers your read bandwidth. Turns out that that in practice,
cues.zh: 我们有这种即时清零技术，可以直接把缓存行清零而无需真正读取内存，从而降低读取带宽。事实证明在实践中，

cues.en: very measurable, very real,
cues.zh: 效果非常明显、非常确切，

cues.en: 30% reduction in bandwidth.
cues.zh: 能减少 30% 的带宽占用。

cues.en: That's a big ticket pile of bandwidth reduction.
cues.zh: 这可是一大笔可观的带宽降幅。

cues.en: We have stack allocation support which is essentially escape detection as opposed to
cues.zh: 我们支持栈上分配，其本质是“逃逸检测”，而不是

cues.en: there's a lot of literature about escape analysis. This is much more effective.
cues.zh: 文献里常提到的“逃逸分析”。这种方式要有效得多。

cues.en: When you do escape detection, you can optimistically
cues.zh: 做逃逸检测时，你可以乐观地

cues.en: assume objects have stack lifetimes
cues.zh: 假设对象都具有栈生命周期，

cues.en: and you're almost always right. And when you're right, the you don't have to read the data but you don't have to write it either. It stays in your cache and you recycle the same memory in your cache and it cuts both the read and the write traffic out. So that's another nice win on bandwidth. We have this very loose memory model which lets us scale the big core counts, lets things go out of order. It's a one way to you still have the bandwidth issue but you can
cues.zh: 而且你几乎总是对的。当你猜对时，你既不需要读取数据，也不需要写回。它一直留在缓存里，直接复用缓存里的同一块内存，读写流量都被省掉了。所以在带宽上又是大赚一笔。我们采用了非常宽松的内存模型，支持扩展到超多核心，允许乱序执行。虽然带宽问题依然存在，但这能

cues.en: you get more time to cover the bandwidth, more hardware opportunities to reorder things to cover the bandwidth.
cues.zh: 给你争取更多时间来掩盖带宽延迟，给硬件更多机会通过重排序来掩盖带宽开销。

cues.en: So in escape analysis, you do a conservative
cues.zh: 在逃逸分析中，你做的是保守的

cues.en: analysis on the lifetime of an object. And if you can prove it has this nice stack lifetime,
cues.zh: 对象生命周期分析。如果你能证明它确实具有理想的栈生命周期，

cues.en: then there's an obvious allocation technique technique where you allocate it on your stack and when your function exits, it's deallocated. So it's free to allocate, free to deallocate, right? Great.
cues.zh: 就有一种显而易见的分配技术：把它分配在栈上，函数退出时自动释放。这样分配和释放几乎零成本，对吧？太棒了。

cues.en: But to do so, you have to prove that it doesn't escape your analysis order.
cues.zh: 但要做到这一点，你必须证明它在你的分析范围之内不会逃逸。

cues.en: And in small programs, small to modest, that kind of analysis technique turns out to work out fairly well. There's a bunch of interesting benchmarks. We get this giant gain, you don't go to your cache, you quit doing GC cycles, I mean, leaving your cache, quit doing GC cycles, everything runs hot in your cache, it's great. For the bigger programs, the analysis gets ever more conservative because the program just gets too big to do the whole analysis. And turns out that, you know, IBM did it on these nice big apps or the one where the people paid real money for real hardware.
cues.zh: 在中小型程序中，这种分析技术效果相当不错。许多有趣的基准测试显示收益巨大：数据无需离开缓存，不再触发 GC 循环，所有数据都在缓存中热运行，体验非常好。但对大型程序而言，由于体量太大无法做全量分析，分析就会变得越来越保守。事实证明——IBM 在那些真金白银买硬件的大型应用上测试过——

cues.en: Those programs get so conservative so quickly that they get nothing out of escape analysis. It just can't prove anything remains live for a short duration.
cues.zh: 那些程序的分析结果很快就变得极度保守，根本无法从逃逸分析中获得任何收益。它完全无法证明有任何对象的存活时间是短暂的。

cues.en: So escape detection on the other hand says,
cues.zh: 而逃逸检测的思路则是：

cues.en: Let's make this thing like as if it's going have stack lifetime but every time you do a store which might escape a pointer out of your purvey, test to see if it's really escaping
cues.zh: 我们先假设它具有栈生命周期，但每次执行可能把指针逃逸出管辖范围的写入操作时，都检查它是否真的逃逸出了

cues.en: out of the stack lifetime. So it's totally optimistic.
cues.zh: 栈生命周期的范围。所以它是完全乐观的。

cues.en: It's totally fix it up after the fact if something goes wrong. There's no pre analysis.
cues.zh: 出了问题完全可以在事后修复。没有预先分析。

cues.en: And turns out in practice, for these big app servers, we can get between 60%, 70% of all objects stack allocated
cues.zh: 而实际中，对于这些大型应用服务器，我们可以让所有对象中 60% 到 70% 在栈上分配

cues.en: whereas the good escape analyses are like well under 20%, 30%. They're like down in the noise kind of range.
cues.zh: 而好的逃逸分析只有 20%、30% 以下。基本落在噪声区间里。

cues.en: So, yes, it's a big difference.
cues.zh: 所以，是的，差别很大。

cues.en: Yeah, okay. So, yeah. Well, I have a nice big talk on how that is and why it works and why it's useful but
cues.zh: 对，好。所以，嗯。我有一场很好的长篇演讲，讲这是怎么回事、为什么有效、为什么有用，但

cues.en: too much in this talk already. Okay, so other things we play here. Supports for lots of cache misses, I mentioned that before. Similar to sort of Niagara model instead of having one uber fast core, you have lots and lots of cores that each independently are spewing out cache misses and then all those cache accesses or misses are all coming back in parallel. And so you get a big bandwidth to memory effectively out of it but you have to do it by having all these different threads that are all running in their own little direction, right? So the goal is throughput. It's not single threaded performance and we really built a throughput machine.
cues.zh: 这场演讲里已经塞太多了。好，那我们这里还做了些别的事。支持大量缓存未命中，我之前提过。类似 Niagara 模型：不是只有一个超快核心，而是有大量核心，每个核心都独立不断产生缓存未命中，然后所有这些缓存访问或未命中都并行返回。这样你实际上能获得很大的内存带宽，但必须靠这些各自朝不同方向运行的不同线程来实现，对吧？所以目标是吞吐量，不是单线程性能；我们真的造了一台吞吐量机器。

cues.en: We have lots of memory controllers, there's four per chip. We stripe the memory accesses across all the chips so you don't hotspot any individual memory controller.
cues.zh: 我们有很多内存控制器，每块芯片四个。我们把内存访问条带化分布到所有芯片上，这样就不会让任何单个内存控制器成为热点。

cues.en: So if you're, you know, successfully accessing
cues.zh: 所以如果你，你知道，成功访问

cues.en: addresses in memory in actual hardware implementation, those will go to all the different memory controllers
cues.zh: 实际硬件实现中的内存地址，这些访问会发往所有不同的内存控制器

cues.en: in a hashed semi random fashion and then come back to you. So the one chip will light up all your memory controllers
cues.zh: 以哈希化的半随机方式，然后再返回给你。所以一块芯片会让所有内存控制器都亮起来

cues.en: and so all the chips in turn will take, you know, their time their turn lighting up all the memory controls. So it really spreads the effort going to memory out
cues.zh: 于是所有芯片也会轮流，你知道，轮到它们让所有内存控制器都亮起来。所以这确实把访问内存的压力分散开了

cues.en: so that avoids hotspots and lets you use all the bandwidth you have. And, you know, one of the observations here is that there is no sane memory layout of local and remote of, I'm going to use all of this chunk of memory and none of that chunk, so move this chunk close to me. You can't do that in business logic Java, there's no sane memory layout. Since there's no sane layout, if it's just random, then, you know, 15, 16 of your memory is on the other memory controls on the other chip, right? It's remote.
cues.zh: 这样避免了热点，也让你能用上全部带宽。而且，你知道，这里的一个观察是：本地和远程并没有合理的内存布局——比如我要用这一整块内存、不用那一块，所以把这块挪近我。在业务逻辑 Java 里你做不到这一点，根本没有合理的内存布局。既然没有合理布局，如果全随机，那么你知道，你的内存有 15/16 在另一块芯片的其他内存控制器上，对吧？那是远程的。

cues.en: So then if you speed up the local case, you speed up the onesixteenth case and like what's the point of that? So at that point, we gave it up and just said, Even local memory just loop back off the chip, come back on, same cost as going remote.
cues.zh: 那么如果你加速本地访问，也只是加速了 1/16 的情况，这有什么意义？所以那时我们就放弃了，干脆说：连本地内存也让它们绕出芯片再回来，成本和走远程一样。

cues.en: But there's no gain either,
cues.zh: 但这样也没有收益，

cues.en: no gain, no loss, it's the same cost.
cues.zh: 没收益，也没损失，成本一样。

cues.en: It turns out there are other uses where you want caches, they work great for your stacks, for your young new gen objects, couple other cases where you want a cache and for everything else, we just do bandwidth at it.
cues.zh: 原来还有其他地方需要缓存：它们对栈、对新生代对象效果很好；还有几种需要缓存的场景，而其他所有情况，我们就靠带宽硬扛。

cues.en: All right, what else can we do?
cues.zh: 好，我们还能做什么？

cues.en: Short cache lines to avoid false sharing, some of the bandwidth saver, we have these nice short cache lines also allows more concurrency because it avoids some false sharing issues.
cues.zh: 短缓存行可避免伪共享，也算一种节省带宽的手段；这些短缓存行还能提升并发，因为它避免了一些伪共享问题。

cues.en: Support for faster virtual calls,
cues.zh: 支持更快的虚调用，

cues.en: we went ahead and put metadata
cues.zh: 我们进一步把元数据

cues.en: in the pointers. We have a 64 bit pointer, we threw an extra few bits like no everyone else on the planet implements the six
cues.zh: 放进指针里。我们用的是 64 位指针，又额外塞了几个位——这跟地球上其他实现都不一样。

cues.en: like the lower 40, 42 addressing bits, that's already a couple terabytes of memory. The upper 20 bits, they just see they have all zeros or all ones. We said, Well, we'll put some data in those bits, right? And the hardware will strip them out when it goes out to the address buses.
cues.zh: 比如低 40 或 42 位用于寻址，那已经有几 TB 内存了。高 20 位，别人只看到它们全是 0 或全是 1。我们说，那好，我们就把一些数据放进这些位里，对吧？硬件把它们送到地址总线时会把这些位剥掉。

cues.en: But we got data in the pointers. And the metadata in the pointers, we got some in for the garbage collection, I'll talk some about that in a minute.
cues.zh: 但我们在指针里放了数据。指针里的元数据，有一部分是给垃圾回收用的，我稍后会讲一些。

cues.en: But we can also use it to speed up virtual calls because those have to do a predicted subclass test and we can put the class of an object in the header and do the test straight on the object pointer itself and not off the contents of the pointer, right? Bunch of little stuff.
cues.zh: 但我们也可以用它来加速虚调用，因为虚调用得做预测性子类测试；我们可以把对象所属的类放在对象头里，直接在对象指针本身上做测试，而不是去读指针指向的内容，对吧？一堆小改进。

cues.en: Cooperative self suspension is actually kind of a big ticket item.
cues.zh: 协作式自挂起其实算是个重头戏。

cues.en: We're going to safe point thousands of runnable threads, not just thousands of threads where most are blocked in IO, thousands of running threads have to come to a safe point and allow GC so we have some cooperative self suspension mechanism where we can halt thousands of running threads in milliseconds and get them to all agree that we're all stopped
cues.zh: 我们要让数千个可运行线程进入安全点，不只是数千个大多阻塞在 IO 的线程；数千个正在运行的线程必须到达安全点并允许 GC，所以我们有协作式自挂起机制，能在毫秒内暂停数千个运行中的线程，并让它们都同意已经全部停下

cues.en: or start our conversely all started again.
cues.zh: 或者反过来，让它们全部再次启动。

cues.en: Okay. So I had a lot of fun conversations through the years with the guys, the harbor guys on how to do all this kind of stuff, right? And so routinely I had, you know, especially when I started here,
cues.zh: 好。这些年来，我跟硬件那边的人有过很多有趣的对话，聊怎么做这类东西，对吧？所以经常会有——尤其是刚来这里时——

cues.en: I had games where I'd play like, Gosh, I really wish I had an instruction that did X, whatever X was. And I go to the harbor guy, said, Can you give me instructions to do this? He said, Sure, I'll give you one. It's about three clocks and here are three one clock instructions that do x. And now, the harbor guy says, you know, And now tell me why it really has to be faster than three clocks. Is it so fast? Is it so common? Is it so whatever? You need to beat three clocks? And I'd have to come back and say, Well, you know, no, I don't really need it faster than three clocks. It comes around every few thousand instructions, so one, two or three, you know, no big deal. So out of that comes this really clean architecture where I didn't get what I wanted a lot of the time.
cues.zh: 我常玩那种脑内游戏：天哪，我真希望有条指令能做 X，不管 X 是什么。然后我去找硬件工程师，说，你能给我条指令做这个吗？他说，当然，我给你一条。它大概要三个时钟周期；而这儿有三条单周期指令也能做 X。然后硬件工程师说，你知道，现在告诉我，为什么它非得比三个时钟周期更快？它有那么快吗？有那么常见吗？有那么……你真需要打赢三个时钟周期吗？我只好回去说，呃，你知道，不，我并不真的需要它比三个时钟周期更快。它每几千条指令才出现一次，所以一个、两个还是三个周期，你知道，没什么大不了。于是就有了这种非常干净的架构，虽然很多时候我并没有得到我想要的东西。

cues.en: But I got a simple chip which is easy to use. And in exchange, I got comments back from them like, We can do really cool things in hardware like directly execute byte codes. You know, the old, I don't know, MIPS was it MIPS guys who did it? Jython? No, Jezelle.
cues.zh: 但我拿到的是一款简单易用的芯片。作为交换，他们给我的反馈是：“我们可以在硬件上做很酷的事情，比如直接执行字节码。”你知道，以前那种……我不记得了，是 MIPS 的人搞的吗？Jython？不，是 Jezelle。

cues.en: One of these Pico Java thingies
cues.zh: 或者是 PicoJava 之类的东西，

cues.en: and I was like, Oh my God, don't do that.
cues.zh: 我当时心想：天哪，千万别这么搞。

cues.en: It's been tried before, it's disastrous. We're going to JIT. Give me a nice JIT target, nice three address risk, make you pretty code for it and it'll run really fast. Don't try and screw around with executing byte codes directly because after a JIT, you won't care for it and in any case, you can't handle all the byte codes so you'll have to bail out the software all over anyhow.
cues.zh: 以前有人试过，结果是灾难性的。我们是要用 JIT 的。给我一个好用的 JIT 目标架构，优秀的简单三地址 RISC，给你生成漂亮的机器码，它就能跑得飞快。别瞎折腾直接执行字节码了，因为有了 JIT 后你根本不需要它，而且无论如何你也不可能处理所有字节码，到头来还是得退回到软件去处理。

cues.en: So we can put in fancy branch target buffers to speed up virtual calls. And again, I was like, you know,
cues.zh: “那我们可以加入花哨的分支目标缓冲器，来加速虚函数调用。”而我又是那样想，你知道，

cues.en: if I look at the instruction traces, the number of times I do a jump register is like next to none because we have these nice things called inline caches. So we don't do direct register jumps.
cues.zh: 如果看指令追踪，执行寄存器跳转的次数几乎为零，因为我们有内联缓存这种好东西。所以我们并不做直接的寄存器跳转。

cues.en: Instead, do inline caches almost everywhere and all I want is standard branch prediction hardware. Don't get me anything fancy. Basic stuff is more important to get right. I'd rather have a 5% bump in clock rate over any one of these other things.
cues.zh: 相反，我们几乎到处都用内联缓存，我想要的只是标准的分支预测硬件。别搞那些花哨的。把基础功能做好更重要。比起那些东西，我宁愿要 5% 的主频提升。

cues.en: So it's kind of fun games going back and forth.
cues.zh: 所以像这种来来回回的拉扯还挺有意思的。

cues.en: Really, the core design philosophy boiled down to what can we do easier in hardware than in software and vice versa, right? So in hardware,
cues.zh: 实际上，核心设计哲学归结为：硬件比软件更容易做好什么，反过来软件又更擅长什么，对吧？所以在硬件上，

cues.en: it's easy to detect
cues.zh: 很容易检测出

cues.en: interestingly bad situations
cues.zh: 某些耐人寻味的糟糕情况，

cues.en: such as cache lines getting kicked out for your hardware transactional memory. You lost line out of your cache, that's really hard to do in software. People who write software transaction memory systems doing roughly the same kind of thing see a 10x slowdown
cues.zh: 比如硬件事务内存中的缓存行被逐出。你的缓存行丢失了，这在软件里是极难检测的。编写软件事务内存系统的人做大致相同的事情时，性能会慢上 10 倍，

cues.en: to do it all in software. It's a tough thing to do in software. Hardware can do it for free, they have to do it anyhow. That's part of their cache coherency protocol. So it was just like a freebie from them. How about cache line zero?
cues.zh: 全靠软件来做太难了。硬件却可以白送这个功能，因为反正它们也必须做。这是缓存一致性协议的一部分。所以这就像是硬件送的顺手人情。那缓存行清零呢？

cues.en: We don't have it. Ours does not order with the standard memory fences
cues.zh: 我们没有这个。我们的实现不会按标准内存屏障排序，

cues.en: because
cues.zh: 因为

cues.en: if you do so, then every time you interlicks a lock with an allocation,
cues.zh: 如果你这么做，每次加锁与内存分配交替发生时，

cues.en: then your pipeline of incoming zeroings gets stalled
cues.zh: 随之而来的清零流水线就会被停顿，

cues.en: for the lock.
cues.zh: 被锁卡住。

cues.en: And so, in fact, you don't get the gain you're looking for. You get instead
cues.zh: 如此一来，实际上你根本得不到预期的收益。相反，

cues.en: instead of of getting the bandwidth covering issue you're looking for which really is you stall the CPU so you don't actually make progress as fast as you were before. Your bandwidth goes down because you're not making progress.
cues.zh: 你非但没有解决预期的带宽掩盖问题，反而让 CPU 停顿了，实际执行根本没有以前快。因为进度停滞，你的带宽反而下降了。

cues.en: So we have this funny thing where here's a write to memory, it's going to zero some lines in your cache and that's outside your coherency domain and you have to do something special about it in the hard software. There's always games around
cues.zh: 所以就有了这种怪事：这里发生了一次内存写入，将缓存中的某些行清零，而这脱离了一致性域，你必须在软件里做特殊处理。围绕着

cues.en: using cache line zero in sort of a speculative way
cues.zh: 以某种投机方式使用缓存行清零，

cues.en: knowing that he's going to get some zeros in but if he has to abort and retry a hardware transactional memory attempt or something, the zeroing in memory is going to be different.
cues.zh: 明知能写入一些零，但如果必须中止并重试硬件事务内存尝试之类的操作，内存中的清零状态就会变得不同。

cues.en: GC barriers for read and write barriers, that's a big ticket item.
cues.zh: 读写屏障这类 GC 屏障，是一项重头戏。

cues.en: People who do academic papers on read barriers
cues.zh: 写读屏障相关学术论文的人

cues.en: typically report slowdowns in between the 10 to 20% range
cues.zh: 通常报告的性能下降在 10% 到 20% 之间

cues.en: and for us then a GC barrier is essentially free now. It's not quite free but it's very close to free. That, by the way, I'll talk more about when I get to GC. That about that read barrier allows us to change GC algorithms to one which scales to insanely high levels and works really, really well.
cues.zh: 而对我们来说，现在的 GC 屏障基本可以说是零开销。虽说不是完全没有，但已经非常接近了。顺便说一句，讲到 GC 时我还会细说。正是这种读屏障让我们能更换 GC 算法，换成一个扩展性极高、表现极其出色的算法。

cues.en: Stack lifetime,
cues.zh: 栈生命周期，

cues.en: another, you know, fancy write barrier detection thing,
cues.zh: 还有一种挺花哨的写屏障检测机制，

cues.en: the predicted virtual call for doing your type subchecking on objects on virtual calls, all done where you do detection in the hardware. And in the software, you do all the complex fix up logic. So there's no register rollbacks on hardware transactional memory for instance.
cues.zh: 用于虚调用时做对象类型子检查的预测虚调用，全都把检测放在硬件里做。而在软件里，去处理所有复杂的修复逻辑。比如在硬件事务内存上，就完全不需要寄存器回滚。

cues.en: Some of the other most of the other academic papers expect you to have out of order engine in your hardware which means you have all this register renaming gear so you can do speculative register updates and then blow them back and reroll them and retry them in your hardware. And we don't have that fancy hardware but we don't need it either.
cues.zh: 其他大多数学术论文都指望硬件里有乱序执行引擎，这意味着你得有一整套寄存器重命名机制，才能在硬件中做投机性寄存器更新、撤销、回滚和重试。我们没有这种花哨的硬件，但也根本不需要。

cues.en: So we don't have
cues.zh: 所以我们没有

cues.en: register rollback on our hardware memory failure. It's all done entirely in software.
cues.zh: 硬件内存失败时的寄存器回滚，这一切完全是在软件里完成的。

cues.en: Relocating objects for GC,
cues.zh: 为 GC 重定位对象，

cues.en: the software inline cache means we don't need a branch target buffer or jitting so we don't need the fancy piece of hardware to do direct by execution and so on and so on and so on. So complicated stuff, you do in software, simple stuff that's usually detection ends up going on in hardware.
cues.zh: 软件内联缓存意味着我们不需要分支目标缓冲区或 JIT 编译，也就不需要花哨的硬件来做直接执行等等。所以复杂的事情放在软件做，简单的检测通常交给硬件完成。

cues.en: Okay,
cues.zh: 好，

cues.en: other games.
cues.zh: 还有其他招数。

cues.en: No way customers buys funny new hardware from an unknown company and a funny OS they have to support as well. So we have a plug and play thingy. It goes in your data center, you install our JDK
cues.zh: 客户绝不可能从一家不知名的公司买奇怪的新硬件，还得去维护一套奇怪的操作系统。所以我们做了一套即插即用的东西。放进你的数据中心，安装我们的 JDK，

cues.en: and you point your Java program at the new JDK and boom, it runs. And literally, it's ten minutes from install to sort of a max score of GBB on any old machine in your entire data center.
cues.zh: 把 Java 程序指向这个新 JDK，搞定，跑起来了。从安装到在数据中心任意老旧机器上跑出 GBB 峰值跑分，真就只需要十分钟。

cues.en: That was a big ticket item for us in terms of
cues.zh: 这对我们来说是一大关键卖点，

cues.en: getting in the door at a lot of very conservative bank like companies, right? We can speed up older Sun and HP gear just in situ.
cues.zh: 帮助我们敲开了许多非常保守的银行类公司的大门，对吧？我们可以直接在原地加速老旧的 Sun 和 HP 设备。

cues.en: Install JDK on your old Sunbox,
cues.zh: 在老旧的 Sun 机器上安装 JDK，

cues.en: it was running a Spark thingy, you liked how that was stable and working just too slow, poof, suddenly it's a thousand times faster.
cues.zh: 它原本跑着 SPARC 架构的程序，你喜欢它的稳定，只是嫌它太慢，唰的一下，它突然快了一千倍。

cues.en: Also, get to avoid all the user visible OS business that leads to, you know, DLL hell or patch hell, right? There's no device drivers. There's no legacy crud.
cues.zh: 而且，还能避开所有用户可见的操作系统琐事，比如 DLL 地狱或补丁地狱，对吧？没有设备驱动，没有历史遗留的烂摊子。

cues.en: There's no swap. We don't have any swap on the box. It's entirely stateless.
cues.zh: 没有 Swap 分区。机器上没有任何 Swap，完全是无状态的。

cues.en: There's no big kernel lock issues
cues.zh: 不会有大内核锁的问题

cues.en: if we picked up Linux.
cues.zh: 如果我们采用 Linux 的话。

cues.en: Our scheduler definitely is a custom scheduler. We got hundreds of CPUs, thousands of runnables. Most schedulers on the planet have never even remotely come close to dealing with that size, scale of thing. So lots of games you play there to make that run well.
cues.zh: 我们的调度器绝对是定制的。我们有数百个 CPU、数千个可运行任务。这世界上大多数调度器根本没处理过这种量级的问题。所以为了让它高效运行，得用很多技巧。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: A bunch of other stuff in the OS,
cues.zh: 操作系统里还有很多其他东西，

cues.en: hard performance guarantees,
cues.zh: 比如硬性性能保证，

cues.en: so you can guarantee individual processor,
cues.zh: 这样就能确保单个处理器——

cues.en: processes
cues.zh: 确切地说是进程，

cues.en: have a required amount of either memory or CPU or things like that so they get a guaranteed lower bound level performance.
cues.zh: 能获得所需的一定量的内存或 CPU 等资源，从而获得有保障的最低性能底线。

cues.en: But the box is big in terms of the number of JVMs on it so they you know, there's a lot of sharing going on but you can sort your processes
cues.zh: 但整台机器非常大，上面跑着很多 JVM，所以有很多资源共享，不过你可以对进程进行排序，

cues.en: by priority and guarantee that the important ones get what they need when they need it. But if they're not using it, then all the other jobs are sort of best effort can pick up the extra memory and make their GC more efficient or extra CPUs to run faster or whatever. Bunch of the stuff, the GC requires
cues.zh: 按优先级排序，确保关键任务在需要时能获得所需资源。如果它们没在用，其他尽力而为的任务就能拾取多余的内存，让垃圾回收更高效，或者利用多余的 CPU 跑得更快等等。还有很多东西是 GC 所必需的，

cues.en: bulk fast TLB mappings and remapping and shoot down, bulk fast
cues.zh: 比如批量快速 TLB 映射、重映射和击落（shootdown），批量快速

cues.en: virtual physical mappings. These are not available in any other OS on the planet so we had to do a bunch of work there.
cues.zh: 虚拟到物理地址映射。这世界上其他任何操作系统都没有这些功能，所以我们必须在这方面做大量工作。

cues.en: We do have virtual memory support
cues.zh: 我们确实支持虚拟内存，

cues.en: because, you know, VMs crash, so you don't want one crash to bring your whole box down.
cues.zh: 因为虚拟机也是会崩溃的，你肯定不希望一个 VM 崩溃拖垮整台机器。

cues.en: We have people ask it all the time, Why do you need
cues.zh: 总有人问我们：既然你们已经有了

cues.en: TLBs if you got,
cues.zh: 强类型安全，

cues.en: you know, strong type safety?
cues.zh: 为什么还需要 TLB？

cues.en: The answer is, Well, you got bugs.
cues.zh: 答案是：因为代码难免会有 bug。

cues.en: Okay, so other robustness things. You got ECC in your caches, you got chip kill, a lot of error reporting stuff, the OS can de configure
cues.zh: 好，再说说其他健壮性设计。缓存有 ECC，有 Chipkill，有大量错误报告机制，操作系统可以动态隔离

cues.en: dead CPUs, dead caches, dead
cues.zh: 坏掉的 CPU、坏掉的缓存、坏掉的

cues.en: memory chips and stuff like that. So we have our own OS.
cues.zh: 内存芯片之类的硬件。所以我们做了自己的操作系统。

cues.en: Why do we do our own CPU?
cues.zh: 那我们为什么还要自己做 CPU 呢？

cues.en: Interesting question. Well,
cues.zh: 问得好。首先，

cues.en: we can't find a multi core 64 bit CPU
cues.zh: 我们根本找不到一款 64 位多核 CPU

cues.en: with, you know, where the design is for sale. Actually, we couldn't find one at all. We had all the features we wanted.
cues.zh: 是公开发售授权设计的。实际上，我们完全找不到一款具备我们所需所有特性的 CPU。

cues.en: You have to have ECC
cues.zh: 你的 L1 必须

cues.en: on your L1. It turns out you want parity at least something on your register file because you got so many of them. You got 32 registers that are architecturally visible, 64 actual hardware registers per core.
cues.zh: 支持 ECC。事实证明，寄存器堆也至少需要奇偶校验，因为寄存器实在太多了。每个核有 32 个架构可见寄存器，硬件实际寄存器有 64 个。

cues.en: You got 54 cores, you're talking thousands of registers.
cues.zh: 如果有 54 个核，那就是好几千个寄存器。

cues.en: You get a single bit error, you're going to be, you know, you want to find out about it, you want to fix it or do something. So we had parity on the register file.
cues.zh: 哪怕出现单比特翻转错误，你都必须能检测到、修复它或进行处理。所以我们在寄存器堆上做了奇偶校验。

cues.en: We need metadata stripping in the load store barriers. We need to redesign the load store barriers to deal with hardware load store unit to deal with hardware transactional memory, to deal with ECC and the L1 cache, to deal with the weak memory model required for scaling and by that time, you're now redesigning about half your CPU anyhow. So we could have picked up, you know, an x86
cues.zh: 我们需要在加载存储屏障中剥离元数据。我们需要重新设计加载存储屏障，以配合硬件加载存储单元、硬件事务内存、ECC 和 L1 缓存，以及扩展所需的弱内存模型；到了这一步，基本上半个 CPU 都得重做了。所以我们本可以拿现成的 x86

cues.en: implementation,
cues.zh: 实现，

cues.en: you know, and chip layout and then gone after the L1, the load store unit, L1 cache unit on the x86 but that have been just this disaster for, you know, how much the CPU you have to redesign.
cues.zh: 拿现成的芯片布局，再去改造 x86 上的 L1、加载存储单元和 L1 缓存单元，但考虑到要重做那么多 CPU 模块，那简直就是一场灾难。

cues.en: And other issues are like, you know, you get a nice high quality port of GCC and the tool chain and all that, but that's only like a nice to have. We totally can do our own port to any target hotspots entirely portable. So we ported GCC to our own chip and we ported hotspot to our own chip and those didn't take all that long to go port. So we have our own CPU,
cues.zh: 还有别的问题，比如你能拿到 GCC 和工具链的高质量移植，但那只是锦上添花。我们完全能自己移植到任何目标平台，HotSpot 完全可移植。所以我们把 GCC 移植到自己的芯片，也把 HotSpot 移植到自己的芯片，这些移植没花太久。于是我们有了自己的 CPU，

cues.en: our own OS, our own interconnect,
cues.zh: 自己的 OS、自己的互连，

cues.en: all that stuff because we couldn't get it elsewhere.
cues.zh: 所有这些，因为别处搞不到。

cues.en: Okay, what else can we do with all these cores?
cues.zh: 好，这么多核心还能做什么？

cues.en: Well, anything we do on another thread is essentially free because we got more CPUs than we know what to do with, right? So we have big compiler thread pools for instance, a JIT furiously in the background. When your big application starts, it's common to get 30, 40, 50 compiler threads compiling, get megabytes a second of high quality jitted code with profiling pouring into your code cache and after a couple of minutes, it's all done and your whole program has been compiled for you on the fly while you're watching it come up, right?
cues.zh: 嗯，我们在另一个线程上做的任何事基本都免费，因为 CPU 多到不知道怎么用，对吧？比如我们有很大的编译器线程池，JIT 在后台拼命跑。大应用启动时，常见的是有 30、40、50 个编译器线程在编译，每秒产出数 MB 的高质量 JIT 代码，性能分析数据不断灌进代码缓存；几分钟后全完成，你看着程序启动时，整个程序已经即时编译好了，对吧？

cues.en: Obvious background GC, we do this giant GC thing. We have like
cues.zh: 明显的后台 GC，我们做这种巨型 GC。我们有如

cues.en: sort of orders of magnitude better GC than anyone else in the planet and
cues.zh: 比地球上任何人都好上几个数量级的 GC，而且

cues.en: we do this by having all those GC threads do their work in the background on other threads,
cues.zh: 靠的是让所有那些 GC 线程在其他线程的后台干活，

cues.en: on other L2s because a standard operation for GC is to go touch every element of the heap and this has some really bad locality. You get you scattergun all over the heap. If you're running a GC on the same multi core chip, same shared cache,
cues.zh: 在其他 L2 上，因为 GC 的标准操作是去触碰堆里的每个元素，而局部性非常差。你会散弹枪式地打遍整个堆。如果在同一个多核芯片、同一个共享缓存上跑 GC，

cues.en: then the GC thread
cues.zh: 那么 GC 线程

cues.en: thrashes the cache that's shared and the mutators, the actual Java threads doing work, all slow down because they're effectively their lowest level cache is being trashed by the GC thread. So we run them all on a different L2 cluster. There's no speed race for GC. They just have to get done before the next GC cycle is done so they have lots of time. So the fact they're essentially running without an L2 cache is all fine. They got an L2 cache, it just happens to miss every time you go to it.
cues.zh: 就会反复折腾共享缓存，而 mutator，也就是真正干活的 Java 线程，全都会变慢，因为它们最底层的缓存实际上被 GC 线程搞废了。所以我们把它们全放到不同的 L2 集群上跑。GC 没有速度竞争。它们只要在下一轮 GC 周期完成前做完，所以时间很充裕。因此它们实际上没有 L2 缓存也没问题。它们有 L2 缓存，只是每次访问都会未命中。

cues.en: And you can do prefetching in GCD. I say easy, it's actually really pain in the neck but it's doable.
cues.zh: 你还可以在 GCD 里做预取。我说得轻松，其实特别麻烦，但能做。

cues.en: The other fun games you can do, you know, background profiling,
cues.zh: 还能玩别的花样，比如后台性能分析，

cues.en: pre zeroing pages,
cues.zh: 预先清零页面，

cues.en: CPUs, hot spin on IO,
cues.zh: CPU 在 IO 上热自旋，

cues.en: clock
cues.zh: 时钟

cues.en: cycle times between when data arrives in memory and when you start processing and doing stuff with it. It's very, very quick there.
cues.zh: 周期时间，也就是从数据到达内存到开始处理并使用它之间的时间。那里非常非常快。

cues.en: Okay. So having come up with the basic design, we have to go build
cues.zh: 好。既然基本设计出来了，我们就得去构建

cues.en: or I guess go design it, something like that. Actually make ideas turn into
cues.zh: 或者我猜是去设计它，差不多。真正把想法变成

cues.en: net list, turn into a tape and a TSMC, right? Hire a hardware team. There's a dot bust in progress. Lots of good engineers on the street. We got a lot of good guys. Hire an OS team, hire a VM team.
cues.zh: 网表，再变成 tape 并交给 TSMC，对吧？雇一个硬件团队。现在正赶上互联网泡沫破裂。街上有很多优秀工程师。我们招了很多好人。雇一个 OS 团队，雇一个 VM 团队。

cues.en: We start porting VCC and hotspot to the new
cues.zh: 我们开始把 VCC 和 HotSpot 移植到新的

cues.en: chip. We write a simulator at the same time,
cues.zh: 芯片上。同时我们写了一个模拟器，

cues.en: eventually end up booting the OS on the simulator and it's actually fast enough to run hotspot
cues.zh: 最终在模拟器上启动了操作系统，而且它实际上快到足以运行 HotSpot

cues.en: on a fast x86 at about 20 megahertz of the Vega chip ops.
cues.zh: 在一台快速的 x86 上，Vega 芯片操作大约 20 MHz。

cues.en: So that's fast enough to run big interesting applications entirely in a simulation.
cues.zh: 所以这速度足以完全在模拟中运行大型有趣的应用。

cues.en: Lots of cool tools rebuilt. Data race detector found lots of real data races both in hotspot
cues.zh: 重建了很多很酷的工具。数据竞争检测器在 HotSpot 中发现了大量真实的数据竞争

cues.en: and in the application itself, get a bunch of cache miss rate, cache layout visualization tools, trace generators, all kinds of fun stuff. I learned interesting lessons here. Your simulators
cues.zh: 也在应用本身中发现了；还做了一堆缓存未命中率、缓存布局可视化工具、trace 生成器，各种好玩的东西。我在这里学到了一些有趣的教训。你的模拟器

cues.en: have to be run on a true multi CPU machine
cues.zh: 必须运行在真正的多 CPU 机器上

cues.en: or you will not get realistic interleavings that will happen in real life. So when we went from a single CPU x86 to a dual CPU x86, a huge count of new data races appeared
cues.zh: 否则你得不到现实生活里会发生的真实交错。所以当我们从单 CPU x86 换到双 CPU x86 时，大量新的数据竞争出现了

cues.en: all under simulation obviously that had never appeared before even though the simulator was simulating a multi CPU machine.
cues.zh: 显然这些都只在模拟下出现，尽管模拟器是在模拟多 CPU 机器，这些竞争以前从未出现过。

cues.en: And that was just you just had to have a real multi CPU machine in your simulator or you weren't going to simulate any interesting data races, right?
cues.zh: 也就是说，你的模拟器里必须有真正的多 CPU 机器，否则就模拟不出任何有趣的数据竞争，对吧？

cues.en: First chip, Vega one,
cues.zh: 第一颗芯片，Vega 1，

cues.en: 24 cores grouped in three clusters of eight sharing a one meg L2.
cues.zh: 24 个核心分成三个 8 核簇，共享 1MB L2。

cues.en: Each core has 16 ks IND cache, four way associative,
cues.zh: 每个核心有 16KB 的 I/D 缓存，四路组相联，

cues.en: extra tag bits for the hardware transactional memory,
cues.zh: 为硬件事务内存增加了额外的 tag 位，

cues.en: the short cache lines.
cues.zh: 短缓存行。

cues.en: The L2 is also four way.
cues.zh: L2 也是四路。

cues.en: People who can do math can suddenly realize that I've got eight CPUs each four way on the D cache and four way on the I cache sharing one L2 that's only four way.
cues.zh: 会算数的人会突然意识到：我有 8 个 CPU，每个在 D 缓存上四路、在 I 缓存上四路，却共享一个只有四路的 L2。

cues.en: So we've heavily oversubscribed the ways on the L2 and
cues.zh: 所以我们在 L2 上严重超额占用了路数，而且

cues.en: we're obviously at risk for false sharing where
cues.zh: 我们显然有伪共享风险：其中

cues.en: two or more, you know, four CPUs all agree to use the same line in L2 and the fifth CPU once used the same line boots out first one.
cues.zh: 两个或更多——你知道，四个 CPU 都想用 L2 里的同一行，而第五个 CPU 一旦用了同一行，就会把第一个踢出去。

cues.en: And then the eight each all boot each other out and you get constant misses because everyone's false sharing on the L1s on the L2 because of the small associativity. So there's a big risk for that but we were at the limits of die size and yield that we could get away with here. This was the biggest chip TSMC had ever done at that time.
cues.zh: 然后这八个又互相把对方踢出去，结果就是不断未命中，因为由于相联度小，大家都在 L1 和 L2 上伪共享。所以风险很大，但我们已经到了裸片尺寸和良率的极限，在这里只能做到这样。这是当时台积电做过的最大的芯片。

cues.en: We did a lot of profiling, a lot of look at traces there to come up with these numbers but they were obviously pretty much a crapshoot at that time.
cues.zh: 我们做了大量性能分析，也看了很多 trace，才得出这些数字，但当时这些数字显然基本靠碰运气。

cues.en: We did have the support for the full 16 chip interconnect
cues.zh: 我们确实支持完整的 16 芯片互连

cues.en: and the L2 miss is roughly the same cost
cues.zh: 而 L2 未命中的成本大致相同

cues.en: as going to another L2 or going to memory. So it's, you know, in your L1,
cues.zh: 无论是去另一个 L2 还是去内存。所以就是，你知道，在你的 L1 里，

cues.en: it's in your L2, it's not in your L2, sort of the cost hierarchy for memory accesses. 384 CPUs,
cues.zh: 在你的 L2 里，不在你的 L2 里，差不多就是内存访问的成本层级。384 个 CPU，

cues.en: we built it and it worked.
cues.zh: 我们把它造出来，而且能跑。

cues.en: It's pretty amazing. Okay, CPU is this easy JIT target that I asked for. Classic in order three address risk,
cues.zh: 这相当惊人。好，CPU 就是我要求的那种容易的 JIT 目标。经典有序、三地址 RISC，

cues.en: 64 bit CPUs,
cues.zh: 64 位 CPU，

cues.en: one hit on a miscache,
cues.zh: 一次缓存未命中，

cues.en: store buffer, it's not really store, it's a store latch, only store buffer, it's only one entry. So it's very simple CPUs,
cues.zh: 存储缓冲区——其实不是 store，而是 store latch，只有存储缓冲区，而且只有一项。所以是非常简单的 CPU，

cues.en: get our masking of metadata.
cues.zh: 对元数据做掩码处理。

cues.en: We have a full FPU per core, that's a very simple one. There's no separate floating point registers.
cues.zh: 每个核心都有一个完整的 FPU，这很简单。没有独立的浮点寄存器。

cues.en: No flags, no mode bits, no weird stuff you get on CPUs that have been around for twenty years.
cues.zh: 没有标志位，没有模式位，也没有那些运行了二十年的 CPU 才会有的奇怪东西。

cues.en: Background spill, fill, register stack to help with fast high speed calling,
cues.zh: 后台溢出、填充，以及用于帮助实现快速高速调用的寄存器栈，

cues.en: you know, up and down, bushy stack call traces. Special ops do a bunch of simple stuff, make it easier, array math checks, virtual call things.
cues.zh: 你懂的，上下翻飞、枝繁叶茂的栈调用跟踪。特殊操作可以一次完成一堆简单工作，让数组数学检查、虚调用之类的事情更容易。

cues.en: The read barrier
cues.zh: 读屏障

cues.en: is a very high frequency operation so it's crucial to be fast. The write barrier replaces a very bulky thing. It's hard to do all the integer ops fast that you need to do the stack barrier.
cues.zh: 是一个极高频的操作，所以必须足够快。写屏障取代了一个非常庞大的东西。要快速完成栈屏障所需的所有整数操作很难。

cues.en: Although, if you're just doing card marks in a write barrier, it doesn't save you so much. Saves you some though. We get our first silicon back from TSMC
cues.zh: 不过，如果写屏障只是做卡标记，节省的并不算多，但多少还是能省一些。我们从 TSMC 拿回第一批芯片是在

cues.en: about 2004,
right? It's not quite dead.
cues.zh: 对吧？还不算彻底报废。

cues.en: It's dead, Jim, not quite. Okay, so the L2s are mostly dead.
cues.zh: 它报废了，Jim，还不算彻底。好吧，所以 L2 基本上都报废了。

cues.en: A few L2s can run because they got the ECC and they're endlessly correcting errors.
cues.zh: 有几个 L2 还能运行，因为它们有 ECC，而且一直在纠正错误。

cues.en: And also, we have this one way, we call it the limp home mode, like your transmission. I don't if you guys know this, but if your transmission dies, it has a limp home mode where you can stuck in first gear and the car will be drivable although the tranny will have exploded internally.
cues.zh: 另外，我们还有一种模式，叫作“跛行回家模式”，就像汽车变速箱一样。我不知道大家是否了解：如果变速箱坏了，它会进入跛行回家模式，卡在一档，但车仍然可以开，尽管变速箱内部已经彻底爆坏了。

cues.en: Like I said, all I said, older drivers are nodding their heads. Yeah, I remember this. These are manufacturing
cues.zh: 就像我说的，我只说了一句，年纪大些的司机都在点头。对，我记得这个。这些是制造

cues.en: errors? So these are manufacturing errors of various kinds that we don't know what's going on yet. So at the time we get the chip back, it's just totally blind. We have a guy at TSMC in Taiwan,
cues.zh: 错误？所以这些是各种各样的制造错误，我们目前还不知道到底出了什么问题。芯片拿回来时，我们完全没有线索。我们在台湾 TSMC 有个人，

cues.en: he gets on a plane with a box
cues.zh: 他带着一个盒子坐飞机过来，

cues.en: and he shows up in our office twenty four hours later and we, you know, score the chips, break them open and put them under, you know, put probes on and away we go, right? And obviously, the first thing that happens is they're dead. Okay,
cues.zh: 二十四小时后出现在我们办公室。然后我们测试芯片、把它们拆开、放到显微镜下，再接上探针，就开始干活，对吧？显然，第一件发生的事就是它们坏了。好吧，

cues.en: what's going on? Okay, so but we have this one way mode, so you have the four ways in your one MEG L2,
cues.zh: 这是怎么回事？好，所以我们有这种模式：你那个 1 MB 的 L2 里有四路，

cues.en: can turn off three of them that are so dead that they're just killing you and the one way lives with massive ECC errors but it's living. So you got a one way two fifty six ks L2,
cues.zh: 可以关掉其中三路，因为它们坏得太厉害，只会拖累整个系统；剩下的一路虽然有大量 ECC 错误，但还能运行。所以你就得到了一个单路、256 KB 的 L2，

cues.en: right?
cues.zh: 对吧？

cues.en: You get register rights from the even numbered registers or bleeding into the odd numbered registers periodically.
cues.zh: 你对偶数编号寄存器的写入，会周期性地渗入奇数编号寄存器。

cues.en: That's kind of really ugly thing. So every time you do
cues.zh: 这真是件很难看的事。所以每次你执行

cues.en: add Rx plus Ry and the register Rz, if z is even then sometimes the bits that you wrote in Rz showed up in Rz plus one.
cues.zh: add Rx plus Ry 并写入寄存器 Rz 时，如果 z 是偶数，你写入 Rz 的位有时会出现在 Rz 加一里。

cues.en: So it's kind of ugly. So we get to a subset of the even subset of registers, right? Although we have other issues like the decoder, the instruction decoder treats branch offset bits as registers in parallel decodes the instruction type as a branch but also is decoding the register bits out of the instruction. So if you're branching to an even or an odd offset, you get an even or odd register
cues.zh: 所以情况很糟。于是我们只能使用偶数寄存器的一个子集，对吧？不过我们还有其他问题，比如指令解码器会把分支偏移位当作寄存器，同时并行解码指令类型：它知道这是一个分支，但也会从指令中解码寄存器位。所以如果你跳转到偶数或奇数偏移，就会得到偶数或奇数寄存器的

cues.en: decode and that cycles the address port for that register piece register file and again you get these updates to the wrong bits. So you have to branch to even addresses now. That's not exactly even, it's like the fourth bit over whatever, some random bit that you had to always have zero on a branch.
cues.zh: 解码，并让那个寄存器片段寄存器文件的地址端口发生轮转，于是你又会把更新写到错误的位上。所以现在你必须跳转到偶数地址。这并不是真正意义上的偶数，而是类似偏移后的第四位，或者其他某个随机位；你必须始终确保分支时这一位为零。

cues.en: We still get a few good chips out of all this mess and we have to over voltage them
cues.zh: 在这团糟里我们还是挑出了几颗能用的芯片，但必须给它们加过电压

cues.en: so
cues.zh: 这样

cues.en: that they'll so the registers will behave well enough you can run it all. And so the chips have electron migration issues. The actual bits of silicon are migrating in the matrix and going the other side and so the chips are literally cooking to death in about a month. So it's like, guys have these chip with all this gear on it and this giant fan right on the chip and, you know, it's howling away on the fan and, you know, and it's up and it's working and it's doing stuff and it's running at one third, you know, one third the clock frequency and five times the voltage and it's dying but it's cooking a little bit, right? So we make progress. We get the OS guys to actually get to where they can boot on this sick thing.
cues.zh: 寄存器才能表现得足够稳定，让你把整个系统跑起来。但这导致芯片出现了电迁移问题。硅材料中的微粒在晶格中发生迁移，跑到另一边，所以芯片基本上跑上一个月就彻底报废了。场面就像是，大家守着这颗接满外设的芯片，芯片正上方顶着个巨大的风扇，风扇在那里呼呼狂转，芯片点亮了、能跑了、在处理任务，但在三分之一的时钟频率下跑着，加了五倍的电压，眼看要死掉但还能勉强撑着烧一会儿，对吧？但我们取得了进展，至少操作系统团队终于能在这台“病入膏肓”的机器上引导启动了。

cues.en: They actually get a great chance to test all their error correction codes,
cues.zh: 他们借此大好机会测试了所有的纠错码，

cues.en: their deconfigure
cues.zh: 以及禁用

cues.en: bad CPU codes, all this stuff. They got that all working out in the first few months.
cues.zh: 坏 CPU 的代码等等。头几个月里他们把这些全搞定了。

cues.en: But we go back to TSMC and say, you know, what happened here? It turns out that actually what happened was a bunch of the silicon IP that we'd purchased from other vendors
cues.zh: 但我们转头去找 TSMC 质问：这到底是怎么回事？结果发现，问题其实出在我们从其他厂商采购的一批芯片 IP 上，

cues.en: from the DSP market mostly
cues.zh: 大多来自 DSP 市场，

cues.en: had spec'd it internally at their site to run at the frequencies we were looking at but that was about four, three well, two or three times the frequencies they had ever actually shipped to customer at. So in theory, was supposed to be good, the frequencies we're looking at. In practice, I'd never tried it and in practice, of course, it didn't work.
cues.zh: 他们在内部标定的规格能跑到我们要的频率，但那个频率实际上是他们出货给客户最高频率的两到三倍。所以理论上跑我们要的频率没问题，但实际上他们从没试过，结果当然也就跑不起来。

cues.en: So we paid for this to work at, you know, x frequency and it wasn't working at that frequency. So they had to come back to us and work with them and they kind of figure where they'd screwed up and we had a metal mask spin. So we took the existing
cues.zh: 我们付了钱让它在某个频率下跑，它却跑不到。所以他们必须回过头来和我们一起排查，搞清楚到底哪儿搞砸了，于是我们做了一次金属层改版。我们把现有的

cues.en: wafers of which about
cues.zh: 晶圆拿出来，其中大约

cues.en: three quarters we had stopped before the last metal layers go on and had them add a new metal layer, so you add a bunch of new extra wires. Turns out in all these cool tricks the hardware guys do, throw a lot of extra transistors on the chip that no one has a news for and then if you do a metal mask spin, get to pick up new transistors
cues.zh: 四分之三在做最后几层金属层之前就被叫停了，我们让他们加了一层新的金属层，借此增加了一批额外的连线。硬件工程师常用的酷技巧就是，在芯片上塞进一大堆闲置的晶体管备用，如果做金属层改版，就能启用这些

cues.en: that you didn't ever use before have a need for. So you could just route around. You say, Well, instead of running this wire from here to there, I'm going run it over here and do this some of these transistors that I just left lying around for this purpose and then drag it back over here and that's how they correct all these issues. So they do this metal mask spin, correct a bunch of these issues and it turns out the second silicon is actually pretty darn functional. There was a minor security fix,
cues.zh: 以前从没用过、用不上的晶体管。你可以直接绕道走线。比如：这条线我不从这里连到那里了，而是绕到这边，接上几个我为此预留的晶体管，再连回这边，他们就是这样修复所有这些问题的。通过这次金属层改版，他们修复了一大堆问题，最终第二版芯片的功能相当完备。虽然还有一个很小的安全修复，

cues.en: I think only us would have ever noticed it but we spun it for that anyhow. And other than that, you know, Vega one was alive.
cues.zh: 我觉得可能只有我们自己才会注意到，但不管怎样我们还是为此重新流片了。除此以外，Vega 1 就算彻底活过来了。

cues.en: Two weeks
cues.zh: 两周时间，

cues.en: from getting the silicon to getting the OS to boot, a day later to get Hello World out of a C program, four days later the Java version works, right?
cues.zh: 从拿到芯片到系统成功启动，一天后跑通了 C 语言的 Hello World，四天后 Java 版本也跑起来了，厉害吧？

cues.en: We had a, you know, year under simulation and the simulator hours really paid off here. It still took us a year to get system robust,
cues.zh: 我们做了一整年的模拟，那些模拟机跑出来的机时在这里得到了充分回报。但我们仍花了一年才让系统变得健壮，

cues.en: not just the metal spin things, a lot of true data race bugs that just never happened before because no one had ever seen a system that's out of order and concurrent before. We got way more CPUs than anyone expects. We got way more out of order allowed than anyone seen before.
cues.zh: 不只是改层流片的事，还有大量真正的数据竞争 bug，之前从未出现过，因为没人见过乱序程度和并发度如此之高的系统。我们的 CPU 数量远超预期，允许乱序执行的程度也是前所未见。

cues.en: All kinds of issues with just true bugs that have to be found there. A lot of performance warts,
cues.zh: 各种货真价实的 bug 都得逐一揪出来。还有很多性能缺陷，

cues.en: I mentioned earlier about having a four way L2 being over committed, well it was. We got a lot of conflicts. Heavy L2 miss rate is really bad. A lot of TLB miss rates, turns out that we can fix nearly all the L2 miss rate issues by doing random offsets on your stacks. It was all the stacks were neatly aligned in one meg boundaries
cues.zh: 我前面提到过 4 路 L2 缓存超载的问题，确实如此。我们遇到了大量冲突。L2 缺失率极高，非常要命。还有大量的 TLB 缺失，后来事实证明，只要在栈上加点随机偏移，几乎就能解决所有的 L2 缺失率问题。之前所有的栈都整整齐齐地对齐在 1MB 边界上，

cues.en: and they all would charge in to about the same depth in their call tree and scribble up and down furiously at about the same depth in their call tree all at one mega offsets with the land politely in the same way in the L2 cache. And so all eight stacks will be fighting for four ways in the L2 causing endless misses
cues.zh: 它们在调用树里都会深入到差不多相同的深度，在这个深度剧烈读写，全都是 1MB 的偏移，结果规规矩矩地全落在了 L2 缓存的同一路里。于是所有 8 个栈都在争抢 L2 的 4 个 way，造成无穷无尽的 cache miss，

cues.en: with little random offsets and poof, it was problem solved.
cues.zh: 加了一点随机偏移之后，唰的一下，问题就解决了。

cues.en: We did a little random offset in the code cache, a little page coloring in the OS and a lot of these issues went away but they certainly started out there.
cues.zh: 我们又在代码缓存里加了点随机偏移，在操作系统里做了点页着色，很多问题就都消失了，但一开始确实到处都是坑。

cues.en: It turns out it is okay to have a four way L2 share eight four way L1s
cues.zh: 事实证明，用 4 路 L2 去分担 8 个 4 路 L1 是行得通的，

cues.en: that misrates entirely tolerable but not sort of out of the door. Just took some work to get there. A bunch of other issues with the virtualization layer, I mentioned we are plug and play. Well, we virtualized the JVM to do that. That wasn't virtual enough, it was showing through. We had to fix a bunch of warts there. I made a model performance fixes throughout the years to make life run faster and faster.
cues.zh: 缺失率完全在可接受范围内，但并不是开箱即用的。我们着实花了一番功夫才做到。虚拟化层还有一堆其他问题，我说过我们是即插即用的。为了做到这一点，我们虚拟化了 JVM。但虚拟得不够彻底，底层细节露馅了。我们不得不修复那里的不少毛病。这些年来我做了大量的性能调优，让它跑得越来越快。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So what worked out of all of this and what didn't?
cues.zh: 那么在这一切中，哪些成功了，哪些失败了呢？

cues.en: Well, the chip worked after the second metal spin, right? Plenty of bandwidth to go around,
cues.zh: 芯片在第二次改层流片后就跑通了，对吧？带宽相当充沛，
